statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and r equals the maximum length of an increasing path that contains k. Write coordinates[i] = (X_i, Y_i). An increasing path is a sequence of indices i_0, i_1, ..., i_{m-1} with m >= 1 such that 0 <= i_j < n for all j and, for every j with 0 <= j < m-1, X_{i_j} < X_{i_{j+1}} and Y_{i_j} < Y_{i_{j+1}}. The path contains k if some i_j = k, and its length is m. The maximum is over all such paths; it is well defined because the one-point path [k] is allowed.
preconditions: n = len(coordinates); 1 <= n <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < n, coordinates[i] has length 2; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= coordinates[i][0] <= 10^9 and 0 <= coordinates[i][1] <= 10^9; all points are distinct, i.e. coordinates[i] != coordinates[j] for 0 <= i < j < n; and 0 <= k < n.
